narrative_summary: SPX closed 7,500.58 (~+1.1%) in the top third of its range, re-asserting the recovery after the 6/17 rollover and reclaiming the mid-fib band beneath the 7,621 swing high. The bull skeleton is mechanically intact (50d > 200d, price ~8.7% above the 200-day, VIX benign at 16.4), but this remains a Late Bull / Topping regime: ERP is pinned at the 0.48% valuation ceiling, McClellan breadth has carved a fresh Extreme Fear low and junk credit spreads stay wide, and the Monte Carlo edge is decisively down-first (66%, below every threshold). The justified posture is trim-bias defensive patience — respect the orderly recovery but do not chase strength into resistance while breadth and credit refuse to confirm.
